work: Use d = PM/RT with P = 750/760 = 0.9868 atm, M = 44.01 g/mol, T = 27 + 273.15 = 300.15 K and R = 0.08206 L atm mol^-1 K^-1. The numerator is 0.9868 x 44.01 = 43.42 g atm/mol and the denominator is 0.08206 x 300.15 = 24.63 L atm/mol. Dividing gives d = 43.42/24.63 = 1.76 g/L, which corresponds to the listed 1.79 g/L (the value obtained if P is rounded to 1 atm: 44.01/24.62 = 1.79). The value 1.96 g/L is the density at STP (44.01/22.4), not at 750 mmHg and 27 C.
rationale: Applying the ideal-gas density relation at the stated conditions gives 1.76 g/L, so the closest and clearly intended choice is B (1.79 g/L); the spacing between choices (1.42, 1.79, 1.96, 2.20) is far larger than the 0.03 g/L rounding gap, so there is no competing defensible option. Choice C (1.96 g/L) is simply the standard-temperature-and-pressure density of CO2, obtained by ignoring the 750 mmHg and 27 C conditions, so the source key is wrong. The blind solver used the correct formula and constants and reached B.
